challenge.better_approach: Refusing the clear outright (raising) was looked at: a clear is testimony and the record must keep it (Law 7), so the operator power is withheld and the clear still lands. Re-reading the process tree in the trouble device was rejected: the hand is measured once, in the sender's process, by the artifact door (ticket c2172127d7a4), and the drain runs in another process.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every hand reaching the operator close comes from artifact.caller(); a hand typed into an emission by hand could omit ssh. The emission files are instance-space and written by DiagnosticBase.emit; a forged hand there is outside this guard, as it is outside 1c1b18bac2eb's.
challenge.prior_art: Ticket 1c1b18bac2eb built the operator close on the measured hand; this narrows its condition by one field the artifact door now carries (a9cf64d1f92e).
challenge.real_collision: none: outline 17.2.2 asks for exactly this; 1c1b18bac2eb's two teeth stand (its hands carry no ssh).

answers.falsifier: Done when a clear by an akien hand carrying ssh leaves a cc-notified trouble OPEN with the hand on its record, while the same hand without ssh closes it; wrong intent if clear_trouble's hand did not carry caller()'s ssh field (it does: cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py sends artifact.caller() whole).
answers.from_idea: none, because it is the interim guard outline 17.2.2 names (cairn/devices/cairn/requirements/17-tools.md, -amm), answered at Q#115 (CairnCommons/questions/open-0bfaf0f5aa8b.json); its artifact half is ticket a9cf64d1f92e
answers.how: In TroubleDevice.clear (cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py), the operator close (an operator-class hand empties outstanding) also requires the hand carry no ssh. The hand is artifact.caller(), which carries ssh under an sshd ancestor since a9cf64d1f92e. The clear still lands on the record; the trouble closes only by the notified rule. A red-first proof emits clears in clear_trouble's shape, as test_an_operators_measured_clear_closes.py does.
answers.traces_to: Law 6: the operator close is an owner's power, and a CC classed akien over ssh would wield it ambiently. Outline 17.2.2 (-amm).
answers.what: The trouble device's operator close refuses a clear whose measured hand came over ssh, Akien's included, until CC has its own ssh key.

bullets.text: Guard (a) second half: the operator close in trouble.py reads hand.ssh, which the artifact door's caller() carries since a9cf64d1f92e.

title: The trouble device's operator close refuses a clear whose measured hand came over ssh, Akien's included, until CC has it
